key_insight: The paper argues that "AI-ready" biological data is not a fixed label but a set of properties that must be defined through a few core questions. Its main contribution is a practical framework for evaluating whether biological datasets are actually prepared for reliable AI use.
problem_solved: Biological data are often highly variable, noisy, incomplete, and inconsistently annotated, making them difficult to use effectively in AI models. This paper addresses the lack of a shared definition for what it means for biological data to be truly AI-ready.
method: Proposes a question-driven framework for assessing AI-readiness in biological data.
Focuses on key data qualities such as consistency, representativeness, provenance, and suitability for downstream machine learning tasks.
Encourages researchers to evaluate data readiness before model training rather than treating data curation as an afterthought.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this helps improve dataset selection, preprocessing, and model reliability in biological applications. It also supports clearer communication between data producers and model developers, reducing avoidable errors and bias.
visual_elements: A central flowchart showing the four guiding questions for AI-ready data
An icon-based comparison of raw biological data vs AI-ready data
A checklist graphic for data quality criteria such as provenance, completeness, and consistency
A pipeline diagram from data collection to model training and evaluation
paper_title: Four questions for AI-ready biological data
